13:11.ar: لَهُۥ مُعَقِّبَٰتࣱ مِّنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦ يَحۡفَظُونَهُۥ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوۡمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُواْ مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمۡۗ وَإِذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِقَوۡمࣲ سُوٓءࣰ ا فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُۥۚ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ مِن وَالٍ
13:11.en: For each one are successive [angels] before and behind him who protect him by the decree of Allah. Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends for a people ill, there is no repelling it. And there is not for them besides Him any patron

5:32.ar: مِنۡ أَجۡلِ ذَٰلِكَ كَتَبۡنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنَّهُۥ مَن قَتَلَ نَفۡسَۢا بِغَيۡرِ نَفۡسٍ أَوۡ فَسَادࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَمَنۡ أَحۡيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَآ أَحۡيَا ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعࣰ اۚ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡهُمۡ رُسُلُنَا بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُم بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَمُسۡرِفُونَ
5:32.en: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, [even] after that, throughout the land, were transgressors

8:65.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ حَرِّضِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ عَلَى ٱلۡقِتَالِۚ إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمۡ عِشۡرُونَ صَٰبِرُونَ يَغۡلِبُواْ مِاْئَتَيۡنِۚ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُم مِّاْئَةࣱ يَغۡلِبُوٓاْ أَلۡفࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ لَّا يَفۡقَهُونَ
8:65.en: O Prophet, urge the believers to battle. If there are among you twenty [who are] steadfast, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are among you one hundred [who are] steadfast, they will overcome a thousand of those who have disbelieved because they are a people who do not understand

8:66.ar: ٱلۡـَٰٔنَ خَفَّفَ ٱللَّهُ عَنكُمۡ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمۡ ضَعۡفࣰ اۚ فَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُم مِّاْئَةࣱ صَابِرَةࣱ يَغۡلِبُواْ مِاْئَتَيۡنِۚ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُمۡ أَلۡفࣱ يَغۡلِبُوٓاْ أَلۡفَيۡنِ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
8:66.en: Now, Allah has lightened [the hardship] for you, and He knows that among you is weakness. So if there are from you one hundred [who are] steadfast, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand by permission of Allah. And Allah is with the steadfast

34:13.ar: يَعۡمَلُونَ لَهُۥ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَٰرِيبَ وَتَمَٰثِيلَ وَجِفَانࣲ كَٱلۡجَوَابِ وَقُدُورࣲ رَّاسِيَٰتٍۚ ٱعۡمَلُوٓاْ ءَالَ دَاوُۥدَ شُكۡرࣰ اۚ وَقَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡ عِبَادِيَ ٱلشَّكُورُ
34:13.en: They made for him what he willed of elevated chambers, statues, bowls like reservoirs, and stationary kettles. [We said], "Work, O family of David, in gratitude." And few of My servants are grateful

_wxQdcjzlZ4.title: The Potential for Change
_wxQdcjzlZ4.one_line: The London Muslim Survey and Gaza show a community with every tool it needs for change. What is missing is the belief that each person carries weight.
_wxQdcjzlZ4.summary: He reads the much-quoted ayah on Allah not changing a people's condition until they change themselves as a warning that change works in both directions. He then summarizes the Social Innovation Lab's London Muslim Survey. The community has high potential: it is young, educated, skilled and wealthy. But immigrants struggle once their savings run out, many people feel isolated and do not belong, masjids are not equipped to help, and courage and wisdom rarely appear together. He also notes the alarming number of Muslims leaving Canada, the stigma around mental health, and a habit of describing problems instead of trying solutions. He turns to Gaza: powers now kill openly without even pretending to an ethical justification, and those killed are not like us, they are us. His conclusion is careful: he will not say change will happen, only that it can, because the community lacks none of the tools, only the willpower. The second khutbah uses the hadith of the hundred camels, the conversions of Hamza and Umar, and Umar's four men each worth a thousand to argue that one committed person can carry great weight. He asks people to carry this belief into Ramadan as their intention.

outline.heading: Opening
The most overused ayah
outline.gist: The verse on change is quoted so often it loses its meaning, yet it holds a law Allah set in His Book for us to live by.

outline.heading: Interlude
A threat more than a law
outline.gist: Summarizing the Social Innovation Lab's London Muslim Survey, he reads Allah's promise not to change a people's state until they change themselves as a warning: if you want things to stay good, do not change for the worse. It works from bad to good as well.

outline.heading: What the survey can tell us
outline.gist: Some six hundred families, mostly from northwest London, so the east and south are underrepresented; still, the data gives real information for next steps.

outline.heading: High potential, weak output
outline.gist: The community is youthful, well educated, skilled and wealthy, so its potential is very high; the problem is connecting people, and the gap between very rich and very poor is huge.

outline.heading: Newcomers struggle once savings run out
outline.gist: Immigrants manage the first year or two, then struggle socially, financially and spiritually from the third year, because the community does not embrace and integrate them.

outline.heading: Isolation, and masjids not equipped to help
outline.gist: Many feel alone when they want to marry, buy a house, find a job or face discrimination, and do not know their rights. They do not feel safe coming to the masjid because they are turned away too often by institutions unprepared to help.

outline.heading: Bystanders in their own community
outline.gist: People come, pray and leave, uninterested in community issues because they feel the community belongs to someone else and they are only visitors.

outline.heading: Courage and wisdom seldom come together
outline.gist: Either people have too much courage and yell without results, or they see what must be done but are afraid, especially parents asking about their children's identity and rights at school; many simply do not know whom to go to.

outline.heading: Muslims leaving Canada
outline.gist: In the last year and a half he has never seen so many Muslims pack up and leave, the reverse of the usual. It is not only the economy: lacking the backbone to speak up is a communal problem.

outline.heading: Mental health: jinn, magic and years untreated
outline.gist: Diagnoses remain taboo; people are told it is a spell or a jinn and passed around for years without professional care until it is hard to help them. A broken leg goes to a doctor, and a broken psyche needs a professional too.

outline.heading: Good at describing problems, afraid to try solutions
outline.gist: We describe deficits well but rarely attempt solutions and have no systematic approach, in masjids or out, because anyone who tries and fails is eaten alive by those who do nothing.

outline.heading: Islam is a social innovation lab
outline.gist: Islam came, looked at all of society's problems and solved them through Allah's guidance; we already have the approaches and solutions and need people willing to carry them as what they owe the ummah.

outline.heading: The old rule: power had to look ethical
outline.gist: In the struggle for power, rulers always had to appear to abide by ethics in public. For the first time in his life he sees that no longer cared about: a veto cast with no explanation at all.

outline.heading: Hospitals, rubble and starvation with no explanation
outline.gist: Bombing hospitals, pulling children from rubble hourly, crowding a population into a small area and starving it, with no attempt at justification even from governments that claim to represent their people.

outline.heading: They are not like us; they are us
outline.gist: The people being killed share our names and backgrounds; there is no difference between Muslims wherever they live.

outline.heading: The sanctity of life is not debatable
outline.gist: Killing one soul unlawfully is like killing humanity and saving one is like saving humanity; keep the verse in mind as we watch what is happening now.

outline.heading: Can, not will: no false hope
outline.gist: He chooses his words carefully: he will not say change is happening or will happen, because he does not sell illusions or wishful thinking.

outline.heading: We lack none of the tools
outline.gist: What is factual is that change can happen. Others in history lacked leadership, guidance, resources, numbers or youth; this community has all of them.

outline.heading: What is missing is the willpower
outline.gist: The missing piece is the belief that you are important in the equation of change. One Muslim in a little-known city of 36,000 can spark a different reality, but only if he believes it.

outline.heading: Change began with a few young believers
outline.gist: Arguing big-picture politics is pointless when no one listens to us; what we can talk about is change from ourselves. The Prophet started with simple individuals like Ali and teenagers who had little reason to think they mattered, and change began in their hearts.

outline.heading: Change starts in the heart, not outside you
outline.gist: It can start in your heart right now, unseen. Attending and then living as before while expecting things to change externally is misguided.

outline.heading: One worth ten, downgraded to two
outline.gist: The ratio of one believer to ten was lowered to one to two because of weakness, but it never actually fell that low in the Prophet's lifetime except at Hunayn, where they nearly lost everything; otherwise it was one to three, four, fifteen and beyond ten.

outline.heading: Interlude
A hundred camels, barely one to ride
outline.gist: In the hadith in Al-Bukhari, people are like a hundred camels among which you can hardly find one dependable. Most Muslims do not even come to Jumuah; if they did, four more masjids this size would be needed.

outline.heading: Are you amongst the few?
outline.gist: Few of My servants are grateful: few internalize their understanding of Allah and live it. Being in the masjid puts you among the few, and if the few have no intention of change, what hope is there?

outline.heading: Weight in the years of persecution
outline.gist: You can carry weight in your community, not physical weight. Read years five to eight of the seerah: the Prophet tortured and defamed, companions laid on hot coals, smoked and killed.

outline.heading: Hamza: a conversion with its own chapter
outline.gist: Amid all those stories, every seerah book stops for the Islam of two men as if it were a cosmic event, because of their weight. Hamza's Islam meant Muslims knew they could go to him for protection.

outline.heading: Umar: prayer at the Kaaba openly
outline.gist: We were humiliated until Umar accepted Islam; then they prayed openly at the Kaaba and no one dared speak. The point is impact, not physical strength.

outline.heading: Four men worth a thousand
outline.gist: Amr ibn al-As, stuck in the conquest of Egypt, asked for 8,000 troops and saw only 4,000 arrive; Umar's letter said each thousand was led by a man worth a thousand. After the conquest Amr wrote back that the four alone would have been enough.

outline.heading: People of weight see the need and go for it
outline.gist: They are not distracted, do not wait for applause or permission, and feel ownership because Islam is their story; then one person is worth a thousand. Or we stay exactly as we are and expect a miracle.

outline.heading: Lands in turmoil in his lifetime
outline.gist: At 38 he lists from memory Kosovo, Kashmir, Pakistan, Myanmar, China, Somalia, Sudan, Libya, Algeria, Tunisia, Egypt, Yemen, Lebanon, Iraq, his own Syria and the Holy Land.

outline.heading: What will you change inside?
outline.gist: If you do not want that to continue, what will you do? Do you feel this ummah is yours, or will you keep listening to complaints, make dua and walk out unchanged? He is tired too, but there is a point.

outline.heading: Can: the intention to take into Ramadan
outline.gist: Can is the only word he can honestly use; anything stronger would be selling wishful thinking. Take that intention into your heart before Ramadan.

outline.heading: Outro

39:67.ar: وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدۡرِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ جَمِيعࣰ ا قَبۡضَتُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ مَطۡوِيَّٰتُۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
39:67.en: They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be [within] His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him

39:68.ar: وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُۖ ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخۡرَىٰ فَإِذَا هُمۡ قِيَامࣱ يَنظُرُونَ
39:68.en: And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on

39:69.ar: وَأَشۡرَقَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّهَا وَوُضِعَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ وَجِاْيٓءَ بِٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَٱلشُّهَدَآءِ وَقُضِيَ بَيۡنَهُم بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
39:69.en: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record [of deeds] will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged

39:70.ar: وَوُفِّيَتۡ كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ مَّا عَمِلَتۡ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا يَفۡعَلُونَ
39:70.en: And every soul will be fully compensated [for] what it did; and He is most knowing of what they do

39:71.ar: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا فُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٰبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَآ أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ رُسُلࣱ مِّنكُمۡ يَتۡلُونَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّكُمۡ وَيُنذِرُونَكُمۡ لِقَآءَ يَوۡمِكُمۡ هَٰذَاۚ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِنۡ حَقَّتۡ كَلِمَةُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
39:71.en: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates are opened and its keepers will say, "Did there not come to you messengers from yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers

39:72.ar: قِيلَ ٱدۡخُلُوٓاْ أَبۡوَٰبَ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ مَثۡوَى ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرِينَ
39:72.en: [To them] it will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant

39:73.ar: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ رَبَّهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡجَنَّةِ زُمَرًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٰبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَا سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡ طِبۡتُمۡ فَٱدۡخُلُوهَا خَٰلِدِينَ
39:73.en: But those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it while its gates have been opened and its keepers say, "Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to abide eternally therein," [they will enter]

39:74.ar: وَقَالُواْ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي صَدَقَنَا وَعۡدَهُۥ وَأَوۡرَثَنَا ٱلۡأَرۡضَ نَتَبَوَّأُ مِنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ حَيۡثُ نَشَآءُۖ فَنِعۡمَ أَجۡرُ ٱلۡعَٰمِلِينَ
39:74.en: And they will say, "Praise to Allah, who has fulfilled for us His promise and made us inherit the earth [so] we may settle in Paradise wherever we will. And excellent is the reward of [righteous] workers

39:75.ar: وَتَرَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ حَآفِّينَ مِنۡ حَوۡلِ ٱلۡعَرۡشِ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّهِمۡۚ وَقُضِيَ بَيۡنَهُم بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ وَقِيلَ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
39:75.en: And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, exalting [Allah] with praise of their Lord. And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, "[All] praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds

21:104.ar: يَوۡمَ نَطۡوِي ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَطَيِّ ٱلسِّجِلِّ لِلۡكُتُبِۚ كَمَا بَدَأۡنَآ أَوَّلَ خَلۡقࣲ نُّعِيدُهُۥۚ وَعۡدًا عَلَيۡنَآۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ
21:104.en: The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it

2:165.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا يُحِبُّونَهُمۡ كَحُبِّ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبࣰّ ا لِّلَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
2:165.en: And [yet], among the people are those who take other than Allah as equals [to Him]. They love them as they [should] love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah. And if only they who have wronged would consider [that] when they see the punishment, [they will be certain] that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment

45:23.ar: أَفَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمࣲ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِۦ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِۦ غِشَٰوَةࣰ فَمَن يَهۡدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
45:23.en: Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire, and Allah has sent him astray due to knowledge and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? So who will guide him after Allah? Then will you not be reminded

25:43.ar: أَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيۡهِ وَكِيلًا
25:43.en: Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire? Then would you be responsible for him

7:187.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرۡسَىٰهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّيۖ لَا يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقۡتِهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ ثَقُلَتۡ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ لَا تَأۡتِيكُمۡ إِلَّا بَغۡتَةࣰۗ يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنۡهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:187.en: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival? Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal its time except Him. It lays heavily upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except unexpectedly." They ask you as if you are familiar with it. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most of the people do not know

54:7.ar: خُشَّعًا أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمۡ جَرَادࣱ مُّنتَشِرࣱ‏
54:7.en: Their eyes humbled, they will emerge from the graves as if they were locusts spreading

54:8.ar: مُّهۡطِعِينَ إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِۖ يَقُولُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا يَوۡمٌ عَسِرࣱ‏
54:8.en: Racing ahead toward the Caller. The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult Day

70:43.ar: يَوۡمَ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ سِرَاعࣰ ا كَأَنَّهُمۡ إِلَىٰ نُصُبࣲ يُوفِضُونَ
70:43.en: The Day they will emerge from the graves rapidly as if they were, toward an erected idol, hastening

36:52.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰوَيۡلَنَا مَنۢ بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرۡقَدِنَاۜۗ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ وَصَدَقَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:52.en: They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" [The reply will be], "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth

36:53.ar: إِن كَانَتۡ إِلَّا صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَإِذَا هُمۡ جَمِيعࣱ لَّدَيۡنَا مُحۡضَرُونَ
36:53.en: It will not be but one blast, and at once they are all brought present before Us

36:54.ar: فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ لَا تُظۡلَمُ نَفۡسࣱ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا تُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
36:54.en: So today no soul will be wronged at all, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do

75:3.en: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones

75:4.ar: بَلَىٰ قَٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُۥ
75:4.en: Yes. [We are] Able [even] to proportion his fingertips

75:5.en: But man desires to continue in sin

24:35.ar: ۞ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِۦ كَمِشۡكَوٰةࣲ فِيهَا مِصۡبَاحٌۖ ٱلۡمِصۡبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍۖ ٱلزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوۡكَبࣱ دُرِّيࣱّ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةࣲ مُّبَٰرَكَةࣲ زَيۡتُونَةࣲ لَّا شَرۡقِيَّةࣲ وَلَا غَرۡبِيَّةࣲ يَكَادُ زَيۡتُهَا يُضِيٓءُ وَلَوۡ لَمۡ تَمۡسَسۡهُ نَارࣱۚ نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورࣲۚ يَهۡدِي ٱللَّهُ لِنُورِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَيَضۡرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡأَمۡثَٰلَ لِلنَّاسِۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
24:35.en: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things

57:12.ar: يَوۡمَ تَرَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَسۡعَىٰ نُورُهُم بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَبِأَيۡمَٰنِهِمۖ بُشۡرَىٰكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ جَنَّٰتࣱ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
57:12.en: On the Day you see the believing men and believing women, their light proceeding before them and on their right, [it will be said], "Your good tidings today are [of] gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein you will abide eternally." That is what is the great attainment

57:13.ar: يَوۡمَ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقَٰتُ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱنظُرُونَا نَقۡتَبِسۡ مِن نُّورِكُمۡ قِيلَ ٱرۡجِعُواْ وَرَآءَكُمۡ فَٱلۡتَمِسُواْ نُورࣰ اۖ فَضُرِبَ بَيۡنَهُم بِسُورࣲ لَّهُۥ بَابُۢ بَاطِنُهُۥ فِيهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةُ وَظَٰهِرُهُۥ مِن قِبَلِهِ ٱلۡعَذَابُ
57:13.en: On the [same] Day the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light." It will be said, "Go back behind you and seek light." And a wall will be placed between them with a door, its interior containing mercy, but on the outside of it is torment

89:22.ar: وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلۡمَلَكُ صَفࣰّ ا صَفࣰّ ا
89:22.en: And your Lord has come and the angels, rank upon rank

4:41.ar: فَكَيۡفَ إِذَا جِئۡنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةِۭ بِشَهِيدࣲ وَجِئۡنَا بِكَ عَلَىٰ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ شَهِيدࣰ ا
4:41.en: So how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness and we bring you, [O Muhammad] against these [people] as a witness

22:78.ar: وَجَٰهِدُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦۚ هُوَ ٱجۡتَبَىٰكُمۡ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمۡ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۚ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِي هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِۚ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ فَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ
22:78.en: And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. [It is] the religion of your father, Abraham. Allah named you "Muslims" before [in former scriptures] and in this [revelation] that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer and give zakah and hold fast to Allah. He is your protector; and excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper

43:67.ar: ٱلۡأَخِلَّآءُ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بَعۡضُهُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلَّا ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
43:67.en: Close friends, that Day, will be enemies to each other, except for the righteous

25:27.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يَعَضُّ ٱلظَّالِمُ عَلَىٰ يَدَيۡهِ يَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي ٱتَّخَذۡتُ مَعَ ٱلرَّسُولِ سَبِيلࣰ ا
25:27.en: And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands [in regret] he will say, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way

25:28.ar: يَٰوَيۡلَتَىٰ لَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أَتَّخِذۡ فُلَانًا خَلِيلࣰ ا
25:28.en: Oh, woe to me! I wish I had not taken that one as a friend

25:29.ar: لَّقَدۡ أَضَلَّنِي عَنِ ٱلذِّكۡرِ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ جَآءَنِيۗ وَكَانَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ خَذُولࣰ ا
25:29.en: He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter

16:97.ar: مَنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَلَنُحۡيِيَنَّهُۥ حَيَوٰةࣰ طَيِّبَةࣰۖ وَلَنَجۡزِيَنَّهُمۡ أَجۡرَهُم بِأَحۡسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
16:97.en: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward [in the Hereafter] according to the best of what they used to do

10:10.ar: دَعۡوَىٰهُمۡ فِيهَا سُبۡحَٰنَكَ ٱللَّهُمَّ وَتَحِيَّتُهُمۡ فِيهَا سَلَٰمࣱۚ وَءَاخِرُ دَعۡوَىٰهُمۡ أَنِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
10:10.en: Their call therein will be, "Exalted are You, O Allah," and their greeting therein will be, "Peace." And the last of their call will be, "Praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds

7:43.ar: وَنَزَعۡنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنۡ غِلࣲّ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهِمُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۖ وَقَالُواْ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي هَدَىٰنَا لِهَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِنَهۡتَدِيَ لَوۡلَآ أَنۡ هَدَىٰنَا ٱللَّهُۖ لَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡ رُسُلُ رَبِّنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ وَنُودُوٓاْ أَن تِلۡكُمُ ٱلۡجَنَّةُ أُورِثۡتُمُوهَا بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
7:43.en: And We will have removed whatever is within their breasts of resentment, [while] flowing beneath them are rivers. And they will say, "Praise to Allah, who has guided us to this; and we would never have been guided if Allah had not guided us. Certainly the messengers of our Lord had come with the truth." And they will be called, "This is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do

42ohxdOpb7I.speaker: adnan
42ohxdOpb7I.speaker_note: his Friday Arabic tafsir circle; completes al-Zumar and the cluster he began two years earlier
42ohxdOpb7I.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat al-Zumar 39:67-75 (Driven in Groups)
42ohxdOpb7I.one_line: The close of al-Zumar: they did not esteem Allah as He deserves, the two blasts, the Book and the witnesses, and people driven in groups to Hell or Paradise.
42ohxdOpb7I.summary: He finishes al-Zumar, whose closing verses speak to the heart about a sincerity one must chase for a lifetime, since correcting intention exists only for it. The verse that people did not esteem Allah as He deserves made the Prophet's minbar shake; it applies to everyone, and failing to esteem Him lowers us, not Him. He contrasts Allah's exaltedness with arrogance among creatures and defines humility as knowing what you really are. He walks through the blast that leaves only Allah, as was always the case, the resurrection, the earth shining with its Lord's light, the book each person wrote himself, and the prophets and witnesses, whom he defines as living proof that the divine way can be lived; the martyr takes his name from them. Allah judges with full knowledge of the inner details of every deed. The surah is named for the groups in which people are driven: sincerity does not demand isolation, but the company you keep will carry you to the Fire or to Paradise. The disbelievers knock on closed gates and enter without protest, in pure sorrow, while the God-fearing find open gates, greetings and praise. Allah's promise is proven true on that Day, not necessarily in this world.

outline.heading: Closing verses that call the heart to sincerity
outline.gist: The end of al-Zumar speaks to the heart before the mind; sincerity is something you spend your whole life trying to reach, and neglecting it means losing your way to Allah.

outline.heading: Intention matters only because of sincerity
outline.gist: If acting for Allah and for people were equal, there would be no point correcting intentions; their whole purpose is to have nothing in the heart but pleasing Allah.

outline.heading: Surat al-Ikhlas and Surat al-Zumar
outline.gist: Al-Ikhlas gives simple knowledge of Allah that leads to sincerity; if it does not, read al-Zumar.

outline.heading: Reciting the verse of Allah's grip
outline.gist: The earth will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens folded in His right hand.

outline.heading: The minbar shook beneath the Prophet
outline.gist: He recited this verse from the minbar while describing Allah calling 'I am the King, where are the kings of the earth?' until the companions feared the minbar would fall.

outline.heading: No one esteemed Allah as He deserves
outline.gist: Not one person, great or small, pious or wicked; living distracted and disobedient, without reflecting on His creation, we cannot esteem Him properly.

outline.heading: His grip and His right hand, without likening
outline.gist: Affirm the grip and right hand as befits Him without likening or embodiment; the images teach that He encompasses creation, which He began and ends with a word.

outline.heading: Exalted above all they associate
outline.gist: What is associated may be an idol, a self that commands evil, a person, an angel or money; His exaltation is of rank, not direction.

outline.heading: Why exaltedness is wrong among creatures
outline.gist: Creatures share one station of servitude, made of dust, so one rising over another denies his own nature, while exaltedness is Allah's very nature.

outline.heading: Humility is knowing your own reality
outline.gist: Allah is not described with humility; for people, humility is seeing themselves as they truly are, and feeling you are stooping to others is arrogance itself.

outline.heading: Rivals to Allah and desire taken as a god
outline.gist: Those who love rivals as they love Allah, and the one who takes his desire as his god, have associated partners and not esteemed Allah properly.

outline.heading: Failing to esteem Him lowers us, not Him
outline.gist: His worth neither rises nor falls with our esteem, but ours does; on the Day we realize there is no refuge from Him except in Him.

outline.heading: Allah alone for 'forty'
outline.gist: Allah calls out 'I am the Mighty, the Compeller, the King' and remains forty, unspecified, with nothing else in existence.

outline.heading: Reciting the two blasts and the judgment
outline.gist: He recites the blowing of the horn, the second blast, the earth shining, the Book, the prophets and witnesses and the full repayment.

outline.heading: Stunned: a sleep without dreams
outline.gist: Being stunned is losing all awareness of time and place; the horn is the war instrument narrow at one end and wide at the other.

outline.heading: The Hour comes suddenly
outline.gist: The blower is not reliably named; the first stunned are a man mending his trough, two men mid-sale and a man lifting a morsel to his mouth, because the Hour comes without warning.

outline.heading: Caution with narrations on the signs of the Hour
outline.gist: Scholars disagree over these reports; diving into them confuses people, feeds illusions and tempts them to read current events as the end of time.

outline.heading: The individual hour and the last souls taken
outline.gist: Each person's hour is his death; those spared are taken in turn, the blower, Jibril, then the angel of death himself, until only Allah remains.

outline.heading: It was only Allah, and it is only Allah now
outline.gist: Between the first and the last there is only Allah; we are shadows given a short chance to taste His beauty, and billions of years are nothing to Him.

outline.heading: The second blast: standing and looking
outline.gist: People pour from their graves like scattered locusts, racing as they once raced to their idols, asking who raised them from their sleep.

outline.heading: Why some reject the resurrection
outline.gist: Allah can restore even the fingertips; man denies it because he wants to keep sinning in the time ahead of him.

outline.heading: The earth shines by its Lord's light
outline.gist: The earth does not give light, yet it will shine with His light; the past tense is used because for Allah the future is already done.

outline.heading: Light on the Day of Resurrection
outline.gist: The verse of light, believers' light running before them, hypocrites begging to borrow it, and the marks of wudu; you walk by the light faith put in your heart and deeds.

outline.heading: The book you wrote yourself
outline.gist: Your own book is placed, printed free with no co-author; every person reads his story, and its ending decides where he goes, so write a good ending.

outline.heading: The witnesses: living proof the way works
outline.gist: A shahid is like the line of poetry cited to prove usage; prophets are the first witnesses that the divine way can be lived, followed by those who lived it after them.

outline.heading: Why the martyr is called a witness
outline.gist: One who gives his life for Allah testifies that the cause is worth it; the ummah is made witness over people, and without witnesses everyone is lost.

outline.heading: Even the prophets fear that Day
outline.gist: Each prophet recalls a lapse and says 'myself'; Isa, who did no wrong, fears because his followers made him a god; only the Prophet Muhammad steps forward.

outline.heading: Repaid in full by One who knows every detail
outline.gist: No one is wronged; people ask reward for a deed in general, while Allah knows every intention, doubt and moment that went into building that mosque.

outline.heading: Driven to Hell
outline.gist: To drive is to make people walk ahead, as the Prophet walked behind his companions; the verb hides who drives them, the angels in charge of the Fire.

outline.heading: Why the surah is called 'The Groups'
outline.gist: Sincerity does not mean living alone in a cave; you are sincere within your group, so the question is whether your group helps you be sincere or leads you to shirk.

outline.heading: No one arrives alone, and the gates are shut
outline.gist: A person is gathered with those he loved; the gates of Hell are closed until they arrive, so in humiliation they must knock to enter where they never wanted to go.

outline.heading: The keepers' question
outline.gist: Did messengers from among you not recite your Lord's signs and warn you of this Day? How did you end up here?

outline.heading: No one enters the Fire protesting
outline.gist: Every prisoner on earth claims innocence, but on that Day no one says he is wronged, because they finally see Allah's worth and their own deeds.

outline.heading: Friends become enemies
outline.gist: Companions blame one another, the arrogant and the weak, followers and followed, except the God-fearing.

outline.heading: Pure sorrow
outline.gist: They go without anger or objection, only grief with no escape; they admit messengers came, but the word of punishment was due for those who disbelieved after hearing.

outline.heading: Reciting the ending
outline.gist: He recites the entry into Hell, the God-fearing driven to Paradise, and the angels around the Throne.

outline.heading: Both are driven in groups: choose yours
outline.gist: If only disbelievers went in groups we should avoid groups; since both do, what matters is the group's values; your company carries you to Paradise or the Fire.

outline.heading: A man follows the religion of his close friend
outline.gist: The wrongdoer will bite his hands wishing he had never taken so-and-so as a friend who led him away after guidance came.

outline.heading: Open gates, a greeting and praise
outline.gist: Paradise's gates are already open like a host waiting at the door; 'you have been good' means beauty that is settled and lasting, and they enter never to leave.

outline.heading: Praise, the first and last words
outline.gist: Their first words in Paradise and their last are praise: for creating it, for guiding them to it and placing them in it.

outline.heading: The promise proven true on that Day
outline.gist: In this world prayers may be delayed, victory postponed, the righteous poor or sick; 'He fulfilled His promise' is said in the Hereafter, so do not object now.

outline.heading: What matters is who inherits the land
outline.gist: The house you built will be torn down and even your descendants will forget your name; what counts is inheriting Paradise and settling wherever you wish.

outline.heading: The reward of those who laboured
outline.gist: Like a labourer paid at the end of the day, those who worked receive their wage in full; the only land that remains after judgment is the land of Paradise.

outline.heading: Angels circling the Throne
outline.gist: So many that each circles once and gives way; this is the original order of things, and we are a small part of a far bigger picture.

outline.heading: From praise to praise: the cluster ends
outline.gist: It begins and ends with 'praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds'; the cluster from al-Ahzab ends on obedience of mind and heart through sincerity.

outline.heading: Outro

TUvLTMqLc9k.title: Fiqh of Ramadan (Ramadan Prep Series)
TUvLTMqLc9k.one_line: A practical walk through the rulings of Ramadan fasting: intention, what breaks and does not break the fast, exemptions, expiations, sunnahs, tarawih, zakat al-fitr and Eid.
TUvLTMqLc9k.summary: In his yearly fiqh of Ramadan class he gives the majority positions of the four schools rather than one madhab, noting that the schools evolve and that a follower may take the local imam's madhab for Ramadan. He starts with intention: the Ramadan fast needs an intention before dawn, and waking for suhoor is enough, though he finds the Maliki view of one intention for the whole month reasonable. His general rule is that anything taken in intentionally that counts medically as nourishment breaks the fast. He lists the six agreed invalidators, the things that do not break the fast, and the disputed cases such as inhalers, drops, IV lines and suppositories, giving his own view and repeating that health comes before ritual. He covers who may break the fast (the ill, travellers, pregnant and nursing women, the severely fatigued), the duty to make up days before the next Ramadan, and when children should begin fasting. He explains the major and minor expiations with current dollar amounts and who owes them, including the terminally ill and the elderly, and the manners expected of those who cannot fast. He closes with the sunnahs of suhoor and iftar, fasting from sin, staying through tarawih, zakat al-fitr and holding one Eid prayer per community.

outline.heading: Opening
Why learn the rulings, and whose opinions he gives
outline.gist: Children should learn the rulings early and adults need them to explain Ramadan and help the ill and elderly. He gives majority positions across the four schools, notes that schools evolve over time, and says a madhab follower may adopt the local imam's madhab for Ramadan.

outline.heading: The intention for the Ramadan fast
outline.gist: A voluntary fast can be intended mid-morning, but Ramadan and make-up fasts need an intention before dawn; it need not be spoken and waking for suhoor counts. He favours the Maliki view that one intention covers the whole month.

outline.heading: The general rule: intentional nourishment breaks the fast
outline.gist: Anything taken into the body intentionally that meets the medical definition of nourishment invalidates the fast; knowing this spares people panic over every small question.

outline.heading: Invalidator: eating and drinking on purpose
outline.gist: Breaking a Ramadan day deliberately, often out of anger or a fit of temper, is a major sin; the day is made up and repentance accepted, but the reward of that obligatory day can never be regained.

outline.heading: Invalidator: intercourse or its equivalent
outline.gist: Relations between spouses during the day, or deliberately reaching orgasm, break the fast and carry a heavy expiation.

outline.heading: Invalidator: deliberate vomiting
outline.gist: Making oneself vomit breaks the fast; someone who feels sick should first intend to break the fast under the illness exemption and then vomit. He offers help to anyone struggling with bulimia.

outline.heading: Invalidator: parenteral nourishment
outline.gist: Nourishment by IV, under the skin or into the muscle breaks the fast; in hospital, ask whether what you were given was nourishment. Vitamins do not count.

outline.heading: Invalidator: smoking and vaping
outline.gist: Any form of smoking, including shisha and vaping, breaks the fast.

outline.heading: Invalidator: menstruation or childbirth
outline.gist: If bleeding begins even a moment before maghrib, that day is lost and must be repeated. He recaps the six agreed invalidators.

outline.heading: Does not break: brushing teeth and miswak
outline.gist: Brushing or using miswak is fine as long as toothpaste is not swallowed.

outline.heading: Does not break: eating or drinking forgetfully
outline.gist: Allah simply fed the forgetful person. If you see someone eating forgetfully, let them finish rather than reminding them mid-swallow and ruining their fast, unless they are plainly not fasting.

outline.heading: Does not break: a wet dream
outline.gist: A wet dream during a daytime nap does not affect the fast, and one at night only requires ghusl before praying.

outline.heading: Does not break: non-nourishing injections; caution for diabetics
outline.gist: B12, antibiotics, insulin, flu shots and vaccines given into muscle or under the skin are fine. Diabetics must ask their physician weeks before Ramadan whether they can fast; as a resident he saw elderly patients return repeatedly with dangerous sugar levels.

outline.heading: Does not break: swallowing one's own saliva
outline.gist: Swallowing saliva does not break the fast, even if deliberately collected, though doing so is distasteful.

outline.heading: Does not break: water left after wudu
outline.gist: Rinsing the mouth vigorously is disliked while fasting, but there is no need to be obsessive; whatever drops remain after a normal wudu are forgiven. Fasting rests on knowing what you are doing and why.

outline.heading: Disputed: inhalers
outline.gist: Scholars differ; he sees no problem with using an inhaler as needed for asthma, COPD or other lung disease.

outline.heading: Disputed: eye and ear drops
outline.gist: He holds that medical drops do not break the fast, treating a stray drop like the water left after wudu, since none of it is nourishment.

outline.heading: Disputed: non-nourishing IV infusions
outline.gist: IV antibiotics, chemotherapy or dialysis come in fluid that fills the vascular system, which is how hydration is defined, so he holds that any IV breaks the fast. Others disagree, and preserving health always takes priority over the ritual.

outline.heading: Disputed: suppositories
outline.gist: His view is that any suppository breaks the fast regardless of its content, and someone sick enough to need one should usually break the fast anyway.

outline.heading: Pills by mouth: no opinion permits them
outline.gist: Anything swallowed breaks the fast by consensus. Most twice or three-times-daily medications can be shifted to suhoor and iftar; otherwise the patient switches to an injectable form or takes the exemption.

outline.heading: Exemption: illness
outline.gist: Fever, pain or nausea allow breaking the fast, and with a valid excuse the reward of the day is not lost but held until it is made up after Ramadan.

outline.heading: Exemption: travel
outline.gist: He is lenient on shortening and combining prayers but stricter on fasting: at least 82 km, the travel day itself is clear, and longer stays need care because missed days are hard to make up. A trucker who is always on the road technically need not fast but would pile up days to repay.

outline.heading: Exemption: pregnancy and breastfeeding
outline.gist: Pregnant and nursing women may break the fast without blame, with an expiation caveat he returns to later.

outline.heading: Exemption: severe fatigue
outline.gist: A Syrian refugee doing construction under eighteen-hour Scandinavian summer days asked what to do: intend to fast every day and break only when fatigue becomes harmful, then make it up later. These are judgments between the person and Allah, not for others to police.

outline.heading: Make up missed days before the next Ramadan
outline.gist: Delaying past the next Ramadan is sinful, requires repentance and an expiation, and the day is still owed.

outline.heading: Children: puberty and training to fast
outline.gist: Fasting becomes obligatory at puberty, but children should be trained beforehand so the first year is not crushing, without forcing those too young or making them hate it.

outline.heading: Kinds of maturity and when to start
outline.gist: Physical, social, financial and mental maturity used to arrive together, as with his grandparents who married at thirteen and fourteen. His own view is to start when a child has the physical maturity and self-control fasting needs, usually around nine or ten.

outline.heading: Major expiation: when it is owed
outline.gist: There is consensus that it is owed for intercourse during a Ramadan day; for deliberate eating and drinking the schools differ, and he holds it applies.

outline.heading: Major expiation: what it involves
outline.gist: In sequence: freeing a slave, which no longer applies, then sixty consecutive days of fasting, then feeding sixty poor people, about twelve hundred dollars today. He prefers caution in obligatory matters.

outline.heading: Minor expiation and the chronically ill
outline.gist: The minor expiation is feeding one poor person per day, about twenty dollars. People with illnesses that will not improve, such as dialysis, diabetes or medication every few hours by mouth, pay it for each day and do not fast.

outline.heading: Minor expiation: the elderly
outline.gist: Frail elderly people need not fast and pay per day instead; there is no fixed age. He agrees with scholars who say children pay it for parents who cannot afford it.

outline.heading: Minor expiation: delaying make-up days
outline.gist: Days not made up before the next Ramadan need repentance and one expiation per day, paid once only no matter how many years pass, and the day itself is still owed.

outline.heading: Minor expiation: pregnancy and breastfeeding
outline.gist: Days missed for pregnancy or nursing carry an expiation even when made up on time; he advises paying it up front. The husband pays it, while any further expiation for late make-up comes from the wife's own wealth.

outline.heading: Manners for those who cannot fast
outline.gist: Someone exempt, like his friend with familial Mediterranean fever or an elderly patient told not to fast, takes only what is needed away from people's sight and joins the family at iftar rather than eating openly.

outline.heading: Debts of the deceased
outline.gist: Expiations a person owed are paid from their estate, but the overwhelming majority hold that no one can fast on another's behalf. Better to pay during life than leave it to a will.

outline.heading: Late suhoor, early iftar
outline.gist: Fast exactly from dawn to sunset; prolonging it out of misguided piety is not more beloved to Allah.

outline.heading: Do not overeat at suhoor or iftar
outline.gist: Let the stomach shrink; half a litre to a litre of water is plenty, extra just fills the bladder, and salty or sugary food draws water and makes thirst worse.

outline.heading: Breaking the fast on dates or water
outline.gist: The sunnah is fresh dates, then dried dates, then water, in odd numbers.

outline.heading: Dua at iftar
outline.gist: The fasting person has an unrejected dua around the time of breaking the fast. Break it right at the adhan with a sip or a date, pray, then eat.

outline.heading: Fast from sin
outline.gist: It makes no sense to give up food and drink and keep watching, hearing and speaking what is haram; Ramadan moves the line further from haram, not closer.

outline.heading: Interlude
Tarawih: the measure is Quran, not rakah count
outline.gist: Attend a tarawih that completes the Quran at least once; the Prophet prayed eight, eleven or thirteen and the schools differ, so the number never mattered, only the recitation and presence of heart.

outline.heading: Stay until the imam finishes
outline.gist: Young people especially should stand the whole prayer; people who stand in line for hours for a licence suddenly ache everywhere at salah. Praying in congregation strengthens community bonds.

outline.heading: Tarawih means rest: use the breaks
outline.gist: The name comes from resting between sets; if tired, sit out a rakah, read along or pray seated, but stay to the end. You will always regret not pushing a little more.

outline.heading: Interlude
Zakat al-fitr: amount and timing
outline.gist: About twenty dollars a person with inflation; opinions range from the first day of Ramadan, and he favours giving it about a week before Eid so it reaches those in need.

outline.heading: Paying zakat al-fitr in cash
outline.gist: Giving money rather than food is a valid opinion held within the schools, and the yearly dispute over it is not a big deal.

outline.heading: Who pays zakat al-fitr for whom
outline.gist: The breadwinner pays for himself and everyone he supports, including a fetus past 120 days.

outline.heading: Eid prayer outdoors, one per community
outline.gist: The sunnah is an outdoor prayer with whole families attending; a city needs one or two Eid prayers at most, not dozens, since the point is the community gathering.

outline.heading: Outro

WsB0lW-MW04.title: Ramadan Prep: Making It the Best Ramadan Ever
WsB0lW-MW04.one_line: Working through the audience's own obstacles and goals, he gives practical and spiritual steps to make the coming Ramadan the best ever.
WsB0lW-MW04.summary: Every Ramadan should be treated as possibly the last, and this one carries extra weight after months of suffering in the Holy Land, so he asks people to make becoming better for the suffering their umbrella intention. Working from audience responses, he diagnoses the obstacles: work and school pressures point to missing routine, so write out a schedule for the month; laziness, loneliness and commuting point to missing companions; long shifts and poor sleep call for pushing limits without breaking. Asked why they want change, people name repentance, Paradise and a reset, which he links to Ramadan as a taste of Paradise in this life and a turning point in Muslim history. He insists on what each person controls: strong will comes from environment, eating less makes the night prayer enjoyable, and the nearest masjid is the one you will keep attending. He ranks priorities: the Quran, since Ramadan draws its status from it; presence with Allah, which does not come cheap; and community, because Islam is a team effort. His closing points are repentance from a whole way of life, dedicating oneself as an endowment for Allah, volunteering with the intention that preserves the reward of prayer, finding joy in giving, investing in salah, and fasting with every limb, ending with Musa hastening to please his Lord.

outline.heading: Opening
Make it your best: it may be your last
outline.gist: Come in enthusiastic and optimistic each year; no one knows which Ramadan is their last, and each one done this way becomes memorable in its own way.

outline.heading: This year's motivation: the Holy Land
outline.gist: After months of what has happened to Muslims in Gaza, Ramadan must be a turning point, with the umbrella intention of becoming better for all who suffer.

outline.heading: What gets in the way
outline.gist: The audience names work, school, exams, laziness, social media, lack of will, loneliness and food as their obstacles.

outline.heading: Missing routine: write a schedule
outline.gist: Most obstacles are a lack of routine; write out each day of the month around classes and work, as he did for years before his own routine settled.

outline.heading: Missing companions
outline.gist: Laziness, loneliness and long commutes come down to lacking good company; find people who will call you and bring you along, and let regulars welcome newcomers.

outline.heading: Push your limits without breaking
outline.gist: Long hours and night shifts may cost some nights, but challenge yourself; you can survive on less sleep than you think.

outline.heading: Sleep and mothers
outline.gist: He manages on four or five hours plus a nap; mothers have it hardest with no days off from their children.

outline.heading: Following the prayer remotely
outline.gist: He accepts following the masjid's prayer remotely within the city for mothers, the elderly and the sick who cannot attend or recite themselves.

outline.heading: Repentance as motivation
outline.gist: Asked why they want change, many say repentance, which is his own motivation every year: resolving that this year will be better.

outline.heading: Paradise adorns itself for Ramadan
outline.gist: His teacher sifted the many weak Ramadan narrations for their authentic phrases, among them that Paradise beautifies itself for Ramadan from year to year.

outline.heading: A paradise in this world
outline.gist: His teacher read it as also meaning the serenity of Ramadan nights, the nearest thing to Paradise on earth, which no wealth or leisure can buy.

outline.heading: Ramadan as a reset
outline.gist: Self-discipline and a reset button: forget the past year, wipe the slate clean and try again.

outline.heading: The month that changed Muslim history
outline.gist: Many decisive moments in Muslim history came in Ramadan, which has always been a safe haven for turning things around.

outline.heading: What you need from yourself
outline.gist: Name what you control: consistency, time management, discipline, understanding the Quran; people internalise habits and experiences differently, so find your own blocker.

outline.heading: Act on your own answer
outline.gist: If understanding the Quran would help, attend tafsir sessions alongside the rituals; put the month on a whiteboard and plan around exams and deadlines.

outline.heading: Strong will is not for sale
outline.gist: Will cannot be bought; it is reached through good companionship and the right environment, such as the masjid.

outline.heading: Eat light and stick to the nearest masjid
outline.gist: A heavy iftar makes the night prayer unbearable; come light and early to whichever masjid is closest, since consistency over thirty days matters most.

outline.heading: Ranking Ramadan goals
outline.gist: The audience ranks presence with Allah, the Quran, the masjid, community, setting the deen in order, bad habits and prayer.

outline.heading: Ramadan breaks bad habits
outline.gist: He cannot rid you of bad habits but Ramadan can: it is a large adjustment that wrecks the old routine through suhur, fasting and busy nights.

outline.heading: Ramadan is Ramadan because of the Quran
outline.gist: The month and Laylat al-Qadr take their rank from the Quran revealed in them, so connecting with it rightly tops the list.

outline.heading: Practical ways to connect with the Quran
outline.gist: Follow the full recitation with a translation, set a daily portion to your level, reflect on it and memorise; as a child Ramadan was his most productive month of memorising.

outline.heading: Gates open and hearts called
outline.gist: Heaven's gates open, Hell's close, the devils are chained and a caller invites seekers of good, so hundreds of millions fill masjids on the first night.

outline.heading: Presence with Allah does not come cheap
outline.gist: Connection with Allah is the most valuable thing there is; it takes commitment and consistency, maybe for years, but Allah will grant it to those who show they want it.

outline.heading: You are only as strong as your community
outline.gist: Community involvement ranked last, yet Islam is a team game: a star player on a losing team still loses, so lift those around you.

outline.heading: Why pray in congregation?
outline.gist: Connection with Allah seems private, yet Islam asks you to pursue it in a group, because it is a collective effort.

outline.heading: Look for your heart in the Quran
outline.gist: Interest in the Quran delights him; a classical saying urges seeking your heart in the Quran and weeping if it is not there.

outline.heading: The Quran will save us again
outline.gist: The Quran rescued the ummah before and is its path back to stability and dignity.

outline.heading: Focus on fasting properly
outline.gist: Most of Ramadan's reward lies in how you fast; studying, working or serving while fasting all earn reward as long as it is not sinful.

outline.heading: Fajr in congregation, then Quran
outline.gist: You are already awake for suhur, so pray Fajr in the masjid and use the early morning for your daily recitation rather than the tired hours before iftar.

outline.heading: Pray the full night prayer
outline.gist: Young people should attend the full prayer; the Prophet led long nights of recitation, stopping only lest it become obligatory.

outline.heading: Raising the standard
outline.gist: He dreams of a masjid with two completions as in his childhood; aiming for excellence draws people up, while accepting mediocrity lowers everyone, though it must be done gently.

outline.heading: Point one: repent from a way of life
outline.gist: Beyond specific sins, repent from a whole attitude and worldview and resolve to live differently.

outline.heading: The tide turns in Ramadan
outline.gist: Name the sins you worry about, but use the opening moment to turn a new leaf; good deeds are made easier and bad deeds harder this month.

outline.heading: Paradise is expensive
outline.gist: Paradise calls those who want it, but it is Allah's price and does not come cheaply.

outline.heading: Make yourself an endowment for Allah
outline.gist: Stamp yourself as waqf, dedicated to Allah and His creation for the month and then for life; Allah has already bought your life and wealth for Paradise, you just sign on.

outline.heading: Volunteering keeps the reward of prayer
outline.gist: If you would otherwise be praying behind the imam, serving at the door or outside earns both rewards; if you would have been home, only the service counts.

outline.heading: Schedule volunteers to pray too
outline.gist: Volunteers still deserve to pray; the Prophet taught that those held back by illness share the reward of those who went.

outline.heading: Joy is in giving
outline.gist: If receiving a gift still pleases you more than giving one, you have not yet learned Islam; Ramadan slows consumerism so you can find joy in feeding others.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr on the hijrah
outline.gist: Thirsty in the desert, they found milk at a tent; Abu Bakr said the Prophet drank until he himself felt satisfied.

outline.heading: The gate of quenched thirst
outline.gist: Ar-Rayyan, the gate for true fasters, means thirst quenched: every lack carried through life, emotional or material, will be filled.

outline.heading: Invest in your salah
outline.gist: Salah is not a burden but five daily meetings with the King of kings to bring your pain, hopes and fears.

outline.heading: Practice until one moment of bliss
outline.gist: Ramadan's extra prayers are practice; one prostration or dua that touches the heart, where you wish the imam would not rise, stays with you for life.

outline.heading: Interlude
Fasting is Mine and I reward it
outline.gist: Every deed has a calculable reward except fasting, which Allah rewards personally because His servant left desire, food and drink for Him; the faster has two joys.

outline.heading: The faster's breath
outline.gist: The faster's breath is sweeter to Allah than musk because any sacrifice for Him is beautiful as evidence of commitment.

outline.heading: The first night of Ramadan
outline.gist: Devils are chained, Heaven's gates opened and Hell's shut, a caller summons, and Allah frees people from the Fire every night.

outline.heading: Fasting as a shield
outline.gist: No obscenity, gossip or quarrels; 'I am fasting' is a reminder to yourself, since you fast with eyes, ears, tongue and mind.

outline.heading: Outro
Musa hastening to his Lord
outline.gist: Musa rushed ahead of his people to the appointment, saying they were following and he hastened to please Allah; that is the motto of Ramadan.

outline.heading: Outro

XGEjdid3kWU.title: Ramadan Prep: The Philosophy of Fasting
XGEjdid3kWU.one_line: Why Allah prescribed fasting: taqwa, self-discipline, separating wants from needs, gratitude, empathy, breaking bad habits, and filling the inner emptiness with Allah.
XGEjdid3kWU.summary: Before Ramadan he lays out the philosophy behind fasting. It is the ritual the self resists most and the first to disappear when religions are altered, yet in Islam it remains the year's most cherished month. Its goal is taqwa, which he defines as a simple filter: will this harm me now or later? From there he draws several lessons. Fasting proves you can tell the self no, because only a fasting human refuses food when hungry, and only Allah has the authority to ask it with no one watching; the question is never whether you can but whether you will. It separates what you want from what you need. It resets expectations, so blessings are appreciated and we expect less from Allah and more from ourselves, while hunger should breed empathy for those who fast involuntarily. Ramadan is a large adjustment, ideal for breaking bad habits, so he asks people to list theirs. Good behaviour should come because of fasting, not despite it, just as faith grows because of trials. Using the liver's ability to generate fuel internally, he argues our strength comes from within. Fasting clears distractions so the endless inner emptiness can be filled with Allah alone. Practically, he urges a light iftar and eating less.

outline.heading: The first ritual to disappear
outline.gist: When faiths were altered, fasting was dropped first because it is hardest; even now everyone feels a little worry before Ramadan.

outline.heading: Where the self draws the line
outline.gist: The nafs tolerates many disciplines but rebels at food and drink, yet in Islam fasting survives and Ramadan holds everyone's best memories.

outline.heading: Taqwa as a safety valve
outline.gist: Fasting aims at taqwa, a simple question before any act: will this harm me now or later? It ignores the neutral and simply holds you back from regret.

outline.heading: Self-discipline: who is at the wheel?
outline.gist: We know what helps, have the tools and want it, yet do not do it, because the nafs is steering while letting us think we are; Ramadan returns control.

outline.heading: Proof that you can say no
outline.gist: Any healthy hungry mammal eats; only a fasting human refuses, on the authority of Allah alone with no one watching; the question is not 'can you' but 'will you'.

outline.heading: What you want is not what you need
outline.gist: The nafs always wants more house, car, status and money; wanting is fine, but it is not need.

outline.heading: Be careful with 'I need'
outline.gist: If you can work all day without food or water, the rest of the year you only wanted it; the starving can say 'need', most of us cannot.

outline.heading: The nafs adapts
outline.gist: After two days of caffeine headaches the last day of Ramadan is a walk in the park; the self adapts, we just rarely let it adapt to something better.

outline.heading: Imagining the first Ramadan
outline.gist: Farmers and shepherds under the Arabian noon sun hearing that they must fast every day, every year, and then go to battle while fasting.

outline.heading: Badr in the very first Ramadan
outline.gist: The most important battle in Muslim history came in their first Ramadan with no warm-up, showing Ramadan is a time to be at one's most productive.

outline.heading: 'I'm fasting' is a promise, not a threat
outline.gist: Saying you are fasting means you will not trade insults or let ego win, not that your patience has run out.

outline.heading: The happiest day at work
outline.gist: His first workday after Ramadan, with tea and lunch back, makes him the happiest person in the clinic; fasting makes blessings visible.

outline.heading: Expectations and entitlement
outline.gist: Expect 100 and get 90 and you feel cheated; we resent our children's entitlement but treat Allah the same way, fixating on the one missing piece.

outline.heading: Those who fast involuntarily
outline.gist: Some lack clean water or food; his cancer patients sit before good meals they cannot eat or even smell.

outline.heading: Expect more from yourself
outline.gist: If you managed this much without food and water, you can clearly do more; expect more of yourself instead of more from Allah.

outline.heading: Hunger should breed empathy
outline.gist: The fasting person should be the most empathetic, not the one honking in traffic, and may dedicate a life to being the voice of the hungry.

outline.heading: Do not fast feeling sorry for yourself
outline.gist: You are stronger and more capable than you know; expect less from your surroundings and from Allah and more from yourself.

outline.heading: Good habits need small adjustments
outline.gist: Overeating and reversing day and night defeat the point; good habits come from small steps repeated daily for a long time.

outline.heading: Bad habits need a large adjustment
outline.gist: Addictions are broken cold turkey, not by tapering; Ramadan is exactly that kind of large adjustment.

outline.heading: Ramadan is built to strip bad habits
outline.gist: Done properly it makes a bad habit almost impossible to keep; its intensity is not meant to last all year, since Allah draws hearts in that month, so write down the habits you want gone.

outline.heading: Because of fasting, not despite it
outline.gist: Do not be patient or kind 'despite' fasting; be so because you are fasting, and fix the language that frames it as a burden.

outline.heading: Faith grows because of trials
outline.gist: We believe because of hardship, not despite it; the most tested are the prophets then the most pious, so Ramadan is a mountain of strength, not a weakness.

outline.heading: The idle liver
outline.gist: Constant eating leaves the liver with nothing to do, like idle clerks at desks, until it grows lazy and fatty.

outline.heading: Gluconeogenesis: power from within
outline.gist: When the brain and stomach complain, the liver makes fuel internally for days or weeks; biology itself shows your source of strength is inside you.

outline.heading: Fast like you just accepted Islam
outline.gist: New Muslims describing their first prostration or first fast bring him to tears; approach this Ramadan as new, as the companions did their first.

outline.heading: The black hole inside
outline.gist: Everyone carries an emptiness that swallows food, travel, parties, substances and work and only grows hungrier; only the love and nearness of Allah fills it.

outline.heading: Fasting removes the distractions
outline.gist: If even food and drink are treated as distractions, so is everything else; everyone who finally got their worldly goal found it was not worth it.

outline.heading: Ambition for Allah's pleasure
outline.gist: Stay ambitious, but to please Allah rather than fill the void; one night of weeping in prayer will feel like the most valuable moment of your life, so use food for need, not as a master.

outline.heading: A light iftar, then the masjid
outline.gist: Break the fast with dates, water and a little soup, pray and go to taraweeh, instead of arriving overfull and unable to hear the Quran.

outline.heading: Eat less
outline.gist: Do not pile the day's meals into iftar; break the fast promptly as the sunnah says but eat less, as he has for nearly two decades, and finish the month energised.

outline.heading: Outro

36:19.ar: قَالُواْ طَٰٓئِرُكُم مَّعَكُمۡ أَئِن ذُكِّرۡتُمۚ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ مُّسۡرِفُونَ

36:23.ar: ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةً إِن يُرِدۡنِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ بِضُرࣲّ لَّا تُغۡنِ عَنِّي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يُنقِذُونِ

36:26.ar: قِيلَ ٱدۡخُلِ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۖ قَالَ يَٰلَيۡتَ قَوۡمِي يَعۡلَمُونَ
36:26.en: It was said, "Enter Paradise." He said, "I wish my people could know

36:27.ar: بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُكۡرَمِينَ
36:27.en: Of how my Lord has forgiven me and placed me among the honored

36:28.ar: ۞وَمَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ مِن جُندࣲ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُنزِلِينَ
36:28.en: And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, nor would We have done so

36:29.ar: إِن كَانَتۡ إِلَّا صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَإِذَا هُمۡ خَٰمِدُونَ
36:29.en: It was not but one shout, and immediately they were extinguished

36:30.ar: يَٰحَسۡرَةً عَلَى ٱلۡعِبَادِۚ مَا يَأۡتِيهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
36:30.en: How regretful for the servants. There did not come to them any messenger except that they used to ridicule him

36:31.ar: أَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ كَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا قَبۡلَهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِمۡ لَا يَرۡجِعُونَ
36:31.en: Have they not considered how many generations We destroyed before them - that they to them will not return

36:32.ar: وَإِن كُلࣱّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعࣱ لَّدَيۡنَا مُحۡضَرُونَ
36:32.en: And indeed, all of them will yet be brought present before Us

7:131.ar: فَإِذَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ قَالُواْ لَنَا هَٰذِهِۦۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَطَّيَّرُواْ بِمُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥٓۗ أَلَآ إِنَّمَا طَٰٓئِرُهُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:131.en: But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours [by right]." And if a bad [condition] struck them, they saw an evil omen in Moses and those with him. Unquestionably, their fortune is with Allah, but most of them do not know

I6u2ikWNuks.title: The Story of the People of the Town (Surah Yasin)
I6u2ikWNuks.one_line: The three messengers and the man who came running in Yasin 13-32, with lessons on superstition, paid religion and belonging to your people.
I6u2ikWNuks.summary: He opens by noting that the Quran calls the setting a city of mixed peoples, and offers his own historical reading: a region around ancient Antioch under a first-century-BC king of mixed Greek-Persian descent who claimed divinity, built a temple of colossal statues on Mount Nemrut, and vanished from the record. He doubts the common view that the messengers were apostles of Isa. Moving through the verses, he explains that people reject a single Lord because idols and middlemen give clergy and rulers power and money. The charge that the messengers are a bad omen leads to a long warning about superstition in Muslim communities: blaming jinn, envy and the evil eye, running to holy men for ruqyah, and denying the mentally ill proper medical care. Ruqyah is for parents to do at home daily, alongside treatment. He contrasts this with the messengers' reply that the people's problem is their own extravagance. The man who runs from the edge of the city argues that the messengers ask no wage, prompting reflection on how imams are paid. His defining word is 'my people': he felt he belonged, had every excuse to stay out, and still spoke, and even after being killed wished his people knew. He asks the community for more people like him.

outline.heading: Opening
Qaryah: a town of mixed peoples
outline.gist: The Quranic word describes a populated place whose people come from different backgrounds, not a single-tribe village.

outline.heading: His historical reading: greater Antioch and a mixed-lineage king
outline.gist: The wider historical Antioch region and a Greek-Persian-Armenian king of the first century BC fit the setting, about a century before Isa.

outline.heading: Mount Nemrut and a kingdom that vanished
outline.gist: The king built a temple of giant statues and claimed divine lineage, then he and his people disappear from history without explanation, which Yasin may account for.

outline.heading: Not the apostles of Isa
outline.gist: Tafsir reports naming them as Isa's disciples lack evidence; the Quran calls them messengers, a term too strong for the apostles.

outline.heading: Two messengers, reinforced by a third
outline.gist: Sending several messengers to one people at once is nearly unique in the Quran; they confirmed one another, each with his own signs.

outline.heading: 'You are only human': why people want middlemen
outline.gist: One Creator gives no one power or profit, so clergy and rulers invent intermediaries and idols that sell blessings and bend the rules.

outline.heading: The messengers' duty is only to convey
outline.gist: They cannot coerce anyone; the grand temple and its spectacle held the people, who are easily dazzled by size and lights.

outline.heading: 'You are a bad omen': shirk breeds superstition
outline.gist: Associating partners with Allah fills a community with superstition, and Muslims who keep this up will lose their children's faith.

outline.heading: Ruqyah belongs in the home
outline.gist: Ruqyah is fully Islamic and parents should recite it daily over their own families instead of seeking holy men with blessed hands or jugs of water.

outline.heading: Mental illness needs a doctor, not a jinn diagnosis
outline.gist: Just as a broken leg goes to hospital, a broken mind needs a professional; diagnosing jinn, magic or envy is ignorance that harms the sick.

outline.heading: Superstition in the Sunnah and in village life
outline.gist: The Prophet taught that linking unrelated events to good or bad luck is not part of the deen; he recalls a villager shunned for supposedly bringing the evil eye.

outline.heading: The omen charge as a substitute for argument
outline.gist: Calling someone a bad omen answers nothing, yet it is persuasive; Musa's people used the same words.

outline.heading: Pseudo-science and the threat of stoning
outline.gist: Talk of dark energy and auras is the modern form of the omen charge; the people threatened to stone and punish the messengers.

outline.heading: 'Your omen is with you': the real cause is extravagance
outline.gist: The messengers turn it back: their troubles come from their own wastefulness and mismanagement, not from those reminding them.

outline.heading: Why the man is left unnamed
outline.gist: Reports naming him come from the People of the Book; what Allah leaves out is left out on purpose so we focus on the lesson.

outline.heading: A man came running from the far end of the city
outline.gist: He hurried in to call his people to follow the messengers.

outline.heading: Follow those who ask no wage
outline.gist: Prophets repeatedly refuse payment; he suggests the way imams are paid deserves rethinking because asking for wealth affects sincerity.

outline.heading: Why would I not worship the One who created me?
outline.gist: The messengers are guided and purposeful; false gods cannot intercede or save; the Quran moves straight to his being told to enter Paradise.

outline.heading: Yasin speaks of the life of the spirit
outline.gist: He ran despite three prophets being present because a living heart cannot bear to see people miss the truth; that is the life Yasin is about.

outline.heading: He had every excuse to stay out
outline.gist: He lived on the outskirts, the people were hostile, three prophets were already on the job and his life was at risk, yet he spoke.

outline.heading: 'My people': belonging and wishing them good
outline.gist: Killed for his call, he still wished his people knew how his Lord forgave and honoured him, because he felt they were his own.

outline.heading: We need more people like him
outline.gist: Every community needs people who feel ownership of the deen, give their time, and hold no grudge.

outline.heading: One cry, and the town was silent
outline.gist: No army was sent, only a single blast, which may explain the missing historical record; all will be brought back for judgment.

outline.heading: Outro

2:184.ar: أَيَّامࣰ ا مَّعۡدُودَٰتࣲۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدۡيَةࣱ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينࣲۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَهُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:184.en: [Fasting for] a limited number of days. So whoever among you is ill or on a journey [during them] - then an equal number of days [are to be made up]. And upon those who are able [to fast, but with hardship] - a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a poor person [each day]. And whoever volunteers excess - it is better for him. But to fast is best for you, if you only knew

58:4.ar: فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ شَهۡرَيۡنِ مُتَتَابِعَيۡنِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَطِعۡ فَإِطۡعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسۡكِينࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِتُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۗ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
58:4.en: And he who does not find [a slave] - then a fast for two months consecutively before they touch one another; and he who is unable - then the feeding of sixty poor persons. That is for you to believe [completely] in Allah and His Messenger; and those are the limits [set by] Allah. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment
